questions.q: 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexene is shaken with H₂ over Pt. The product is:
options: An equal mixture of cis- and trans-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane
questions.explain: The alkene lies flat on the metal surface and both hydrogens arrive from the underside (syn addition), so only the cis product forms.

questions.q: 3-Methylbut-1-ene, 2-methylbut-1-ene and 2-methylbut-2-ene all give 2-methylbutane on hydrogenation. Which is the most stable alkene?
options: All three are equally stable, since they give the same alkane
questions.explain: 2-Methylbut-2-ene releases the least heat (−26.9 kcal per mole against −28.5 and −30.3), so it starts lowest in energy. Stability rises with the number of alkyl groups on the C=C.

questions.q: Which group is NOT reduced by ordinary catalytic hydrogenation over Ni, Pd or Pt?
questions.explain: COOH, like esters and amides, is too stable for ordinary hydrogenation. Nitro groups and nitriles are reduced to amines, and an alkyne takes up two H₂ to give the alkane.

questions.q: Using the exam convention that the rate of catalytic hydrogenation runs parallel to the heat of hydrogenation, which alkene is hydrogenated fastest?
questions.explain: The monosubstituted 3-methylbut-1-ene has the largest heat of hydrogenation (−30.3 kcal per mole) and is the least hindered, so it adsorbs on the metal most easily. More substituted alkenes are more stable and react more slowly.
